intro: The ship was crushed by pack ice in the first winter. What survives of the expedition is a biscuit tin full of messages, each written in a different hand, and each deliberately obscure.
echo: The navigator trusted only one star: the one that never moved.

puzzles.title: Dead Reckoning
puzzles.flavor: Only one page of the book survived. Luckily, it was the only page anyone needed.

blocks.text: The ship was crushed by pack ice in the first winter. What survives of the expedition is a biscuit tin full of messages, each written in a different hand, and each deliberately obscure.

puzzles.hint: Each pair is word.letter into the recovered page (words split on spaces; punctuation ignored).

puzzles.title: Ship's Biscuit
puzzles.flavor: An inventory of base camp, tangled up. Whatever is left over when every item is accounted for is yours.
puzzles.hint: Find every listed word (any of 8 directions). The unused letters, read left-to-right, top-to-bottom, spell the answer.

puzzles.title: Sastrugi
puzzles.flavor: The knight never moves in a straight line, and neither does the truth at base camp.

blocks.text: The knight sets out from d5: Nb6 Na4 Nc5 Ne6 Nd8 Nb7 Nd6 Ne4 Ng3.

puzzles.hint: Start on the given square and follow the knight moves; read the letter on each square it lands on.

puzzles.title: Pack Ice
puzzles.flavor: Unjumble the kit list. You'll have one letter left over every time, and you'll want to keep those.
puzzles.hint: Each jumble is an anagram of a word from this round's theme plus one extra letter. The extra letters, in order, spell the answer.

puzzles.title: Whiteout
puzzles.flavor: Knock, knock. Pause. Knock knock knock.
puzzles.hint: Tap code: first burst = row, second = column, in a 5×5 grid without K.

puzzles.title: Polar Plateau
puzzles.flavor: Not a single letter on the page, and yet it says something.
puzzles.hint: Each symbol stands for one letter (a simple substitution); word breaks are kept. Solve the sentence; it tells you the answer.

puzzles.title: Winter Quarters
puzzles.flavor: The machine spoke American Standard. Every row is one character.
puzzles.hint: Each row of the paper tape is a 7-bit ASCII character (hole = 1, most significant bit on the left).

meta.title: Meta: The Last Expedition
meta.flavor: File everything the way an archivist would, by its heading. Then walk down the drawer.
meta.explain: Order the puzzles alphabetically by title; take the k-th letter of the k-th answer.
